clinician.final_diagnosis: Electron microscopy showed lamellated lipid inclusions in podocytes, which were compatible with Fabry disease
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 61-year-old woman with chronic kidney disease and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy presented with intermittent lower abdominal cramping. Initial laboratory tests for Fabry disease, including α-galactosidase enzyme activity and plasma lyso-Gb3 levels, were within normal ranges. However, a review of a previous kidney biopsy by electron microscopy revealed lamellated lipid inclusions in podocytes (E005), which was compatible with Fabry disease. Genetic testing for GLA gene mutations identified five variants (E004). Following the diagnosis, enzyme replacement therapy (ERT) with agalsidase-β was initiated, leading to a substantial reduction in abdominal pain (E007).
